what: Negative controls for tools/save_migration.mjs. Each mutation was applied to the source alone, rebuilt, and the gate re-run. A gate that has never failed is not evidence.
result: 9 of 9 mutations rejected by the gate
corrections_made_during_this_run: The 'no migration is registered at all' mutation was first written in a form that did not parse, so the build refused it and it proved nothing about the gate. It was rewritten to delete the registry entry (valid JavaScript) and re-run: the gate fails 8 checks.

The 'the version is not stamped' mutation was MISSED on the first pass. Every shipped migration step stamps its own version, so the final backstop stamp was never exercised by a test. Two checks were added for a registry step that forgets the version; the mutation is now caught.
how_to_reproduce: Apply one mutation at a time to the named file, run `node build.mjs --dev`, then `node tools/save_migration.mjs`, and require a non-zero exit. Restore the file before the next one. The harness that automated this was deliberately not committed: it rewrites files under src/, and an accidental run would corrupt the working tree.
